description: A hat on the wrong peg

participation.context: Told them to leave the hat, take the cue, and eat before two.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Set the entrance at twelve paces and the cue on "anon," and kept the peg for himself at the half hour.
participation.name: Augustine Phillips

participation.context: Took the cue, and said he would walk the twelve paces once in the yard.
participation.name: Richard Cowley

participation.context: Claimed the hat, got out of the doorway, and stayed for cold meat in the tiring-house.
participation.name: Thomas Pope

relations.note: the cue is "anon" at twelve paces
relations.quote: When I say \"anon,\" you are already in the door.

story.body: You stopped the argument about whose hat it was. You had Cowley walk the twelve paces and take the cue. You left the second scene there, and you sent him to eat before two.

relations.note: the cue is "anon" at twelve paces
relations.quote: When I say \"anon,\" you are already in the door.

title: Told them to let the hat fall and go on

participation.context: Read the plot and played the afternoon bill.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You read the plot on the post. Your name was among the players. No author was named. You went on and played.

title: Read the Errors plot and played

participation.context: Gave the comedy for the ninth, refused a second, and said the king is about to be unkinged.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Opened the almanac, took the comedy for Whit Monday, and asked for a Labour's Won at Michaelmas.
participation.name: John Heminges

participation.context: Asked for the end speech again before the ninth, and set the king for Michaelmas, when the Inns are back.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Wanted a jig after the holiday play, and said a king being unkinged is a long afternoon.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Wanted the ninth written down before the autumn was spent.
participation.name: Augustine Phillips

participation.context: Counted three weeks of old stock to Midsummer, and held his question for the next sitting.
participation.name: George Bryan

relations.note: the comedy is his for Monday the ninth
relations.quote: I want the comedy for the Monday holiday.

story.body: You gave Heminges the comedy for Monday the ninth. You did not give him a Labour's Won. You told them the king is about to be unkinged, and you left that for Michaelmas. You left the rest of the questions for the next quarter-hour.

relations.note: the comedy is his for Monday the ninth
relations.quote: I want the comedy for the Monday holiday.

topics: a king about to be unkinged

title: Gave Heminges the comedy for the ninth

participation.context: Said it is in the chronicle, said the parts are not cast, and named no sum.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Asked about keeping takings back, took the agreement without a figure, and shut the almanac.
participation.name: John Heminges

participation.context: Kept the king at Michaelmas, and refused to fill the eighteen days with another Errors.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Asked what part he has, was told nothing is cast, and accepted that nothing was being hidden.
participation.name: Will Kemp

participation.context: Disliked the keeping-back and agreed to it, and read Trinity term off the almanac.
participation.name: Augustine Phillips

participation.context: Asked about the Master, and agreed to the keeping-back while saying he disliked it.
participation.name: George Bryan

relations.note: a king put down, answered from the chronicle

story.body: You told Bryan the matter is in the chronicle. You told Kemp the parts are not cast. You agreed that takings may be kept back, and you named no sum. You let Heminges shut the almanac on the ninth, the three weeks, Michaelmas, and the twentieth.

relations.note: a king put down, answered from the chronicle

title: Told Bryan the matter is in the chronicle
